messages.author: 30741827d601685b
messages.subject: Strange, and inexplicable, error
parts:
When attempting to run a spatiotemporal analysis, I keep getting the following error:


Error in inla(formula, family = "zeroinflatedpoisson0", data = Rabies2,  : 
  The response for family[1] is not of type 'numeric|list|matrix'; don't know what to do.

The program isn't the only one that doesn't know what to do!

Here's the code and the data file is attached:

Rabies.Project.Init <- read.csv("E:/Rabies/Data/Rabies Project Init.csv")
Rabies2 <- Rabies.Project.Init
WVmap <-readOGR(dsn = "E:/WV.gdb",
                layer="County")
WVmap$struct <-1:nrow(WVmap@data)
wvnb <- poly2nb(WVmap, row.names=WVmap$struct)
nb2INLA(wvnb, file = "E:/Rabies/Data/wvgraph.gra")
wv.adj <- wvnb

Rabies2$NoRRVpos <- as.factor(Rabies2$NoRRVpos)
Rabies2$FIPS <- as.factor(Rabies2$FIPS)
Rabies2$year <-as.factor(Rabies2$Year2)
Rabies2$year2 <-as.factor(Rabies2$Year2)

formula <- NoRRVpos ~  f(FIPS, model="bym", graph=wv.adj)+
  f(year, model = "rw2")+
  f(year2, model="iid")

combs <- inla.make.lincomb(year=diag(16),year2=diag(16))

rabmod <- inla(formula,
               family="zeroinflatedpoisson0",
               data=Rabies2,
               control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE),
               lincomb = combs)

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Strange, and inexplicable, error

The error was about FIPS so focus on that. 
Finn


On 27 Nov 2017 18:22, "Bert Plants" <kbpl...@mix.wvu.edu> wrote:
Okay, tried that...same error.  FIPS is still a factor, year and year2 are now numeric. And the graph file has region.id that starts at 1.

On Mon, Nov 27, 2017 at 1:13 PM, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
Year with rw2 doesn't really make sense as a factor. Year2 should be OK as factor. 
For the graph model you need indices, starting from 1.
Finn


On 27 Nov 2017 18:06, "Bert Plants" <kbpl...@mix.wvu.edu> wrote:
Okay, but all covariates (FIPS, year, year2) are factors...

(didn't work any better when I left them as numeric, btw)

On Mon, Nov 27, 2017 at 12:55 PM, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
On 27 November 2017 at 17:50, Bert Plants <kbpl...@mix.wvu.edu> wrote:
> I did that because I kept getting this error:
>
> Error in inla(formula, family = "zeroinflatedpoisson0", data = Rabies2,  :
>   In f(FIPS): 'covariate' must match 'values',  and both must either be
> 'numeric', or 'factor'/'character'.

That relates to variables on "the right hand side" of the formula, not
the response.

Finn
